title: API: REST OpenAPI / discovery generation
description: IN: generate OpenAPI 3.0 specs from handler getOpenApiSpec() + param/body/response-schema hooks + route x-i18n-* metadata; ModuleSpecHandler (/specs/v0/module/{module}) + DiscoveryHandler; response-schema-file loading (Rest/Handler/Schema/*.json). OUT: per-endpoint handlers; audience modes.
design: Rest/Validator/Validator.php schema/param generators; Rest/Handler/ModuleSpecHandler.php, DiscoveryHandler.php; schema files like ExistingPageSource.json. docs/rest/mwapi-1.0.json/mwapi-1.1.json/discovery-1.0.json are the JSON schemas to validate output against. This /specs/v0 endpoint is the free contract oracle WS7's wire-parity harness (ws7-s2) relies on.
acceptance_criteria: Generated spec for the first module validates against mwapi-1.1.json; discovery lists registered modules.
notes: Test: schema-validation tests against the in-repo docs/rest/*.json. (Blocked by ws4-s1.)

title: API: REST framework core — Router + Handler base + ObjectFactory route loading
description: IN: TS port of the REST lifecycle — EntryPoint->Router::execute->splitPath->Module resolution (ExtraRoutesModule for flat coreRoutes.json + SpecBasedModule for content.v1.json style)->PathMatcher->handler construction via the WS1 DI/ObjectFactory equivalent->the four init* stages->Validator (params/body/header)->execute()->ResponseFactory->CORS; the error model (HttpException/LocalizedHttpException -> ResponseFactory::createFromException); HEAD->GET fallback; JSON-body-must-be-object; the shared ParamValidator port (used by both APIs). OUT: OpenAPI gen (ws4-s2); concrete handlers (ws4-s3); audience modes; RESTBase-compat shim.
design: Templates: includes/Rest/Router.php (12-dep DI signature), Rest/EntryPoint.php::createRouter, Rest/Module/Module.php::executeHandler (the canonical pipeline), Rest/Handler.php (abstract base, four final init methods, execute() abstract), Rest/SimpleHandler.php, Rest/Validator/Validator.php, Rest/ResponseFactory.php. Routes loaded from the existing JSON files unchanged. Confirmed DI-clean + JSON-native.
acceptance_criteria: A trivial registered GET handler returns the expected JSON Response with the correct status/headers; unknown path -> 404; bad param -> 400 with the standard error body; HEAD on a GET route works.
notes: Test: unit tests mirroring tests/phpunit/unit/includes/Rest/; no live data. (Blocked by ws1-s1, ws1-s6.) Open Q: which WS1 DI primitive backs ObjectFactory specs; PSR-7-shaped Request/Response ported verbatim vs a Node HTTP abstraction.

title: Read: TS Parsoid-sidecar adapter — serve DataAccess/PageConfig/SiteConfig over the network
description: IN: the TS service answering the ws3-s1 contract for the constrained set — getPageInfo (existence/revId/redirect/known/linkclasses, batched), getFileInfo (stub if files excluded), fetchTemplateSource/fetchTemplateData, addTrackingCategory, logLinterData (no-op/read-only), getExternalUrlInfo; PageConfig per-page fields; a SiteConfig snapshot; wired to WS2's MCR read model + connection provider. OUT: parseWikitext/preprocessWikitext (hard-fail with a clear error — the constrained set excludes them); write paths; invalidation.
design: Mirror Api/DataAccess.php field-for-field (return shapes documented in the abstract docblocks, e.g. getPageInfo -> {pageId,revId,missing,known,redirect,linkclasses}). getPageInfo maps onto WS2 page/revision reads + a link-batch (core does LinkBatchFactory->newLinkBatch->execute at DataAccess.php:191). SiteConfig namespaces/interwiki come from the config snapshot (ws1-s3). Consumes WS2 connection provider (ws2-s3) for the synchronous batched reads.
acceptance_criteria: Real Parsoid renders every page in the constrained set against this service with ZERO in-process PHP fallback; byte-compare the returned DataAccess payloads against Api/DataAccess output for the same titles.
notes: Test: contract tests asserting payload shape vs the abstract docblock + Api/DataAccess golden responses; integration running Parsoid end-to-end. (Blocked by ws3-s1, ws2-s3.) Open Q: connection-provider transaction boundary for the synchronous batched reads.

title: Read: SPIKE — Parsoid DataAccess-over-network contract & latency proof
description: IN: stand up the real wikimedia/parsoid package with a NETWORK DataAccess (modeled on Api/DataAccess.php) + a snapshot SiteConfig, pointed at a stub TS service answering the 7 DataAccess methods + per-page PageConfig fields over HTTP; drive Parsoid::wikitext2html() for ~20 pages from the constrained set (DECIDED: simple anonymous article views with NO templates/transclusions and NO extension tags); measure round-trips/parse, p50/p95 latency vs in-process, N+1 of getPageInfo (50-title chunks) and fetchTemplateSource; CONFIRM the constrained set never invokes parseWikitext/preprocessWikitext. OUT: production caching, real read path, output transform, skinning; no TS reimplementation of Parsoid.
design: Contract = vendor/wikimedia/parsoid/src/Config/DataAccess.php (7 abstract methods: getPageInfo, getFileInfo, parseWikitext, preprocessWikitext, fetchTemplateSource, fetchTemplateData, logLinterData/addTrackingCategory — all SYNCHRONOUS) + PageConfig.php (11 getters) + SiteConfig.php (44 mostly-static methods -> snapshot, don't serve per-call). CORRECTION vs Epic: an over-network impl ALREADY EXISTS (vendor/wikimedia/parsoid/src/Config/Api/DataAccess.php, 100-entry LRU) but is documented 'intended for testing, not performance' — so the spike is about LATENCY/batching/N+1, not feasibility. The constrained-set choice (exclude templates+ext-tags) is precisely to avoid parseWikitext/preprocessWikitext, which call BACK into the legacy PHP parser.
acceptance_criteria: A written contract spec naming each method, its call frequency on the constrained set, batchability, and measured latency; explicit go/no-go that the constrained set avoids parseWikitext/preprocessWikitext; a reproducible harness.
notes: Test: custom harness invoking real Parsoid against the stub; assert on call counts + timing, not HTML; seed pages from tests/parser/parserTests.txt !! article fixtures. Open Q: API-shaped contract vs a leaner RPC; can SiteConfig be fully snapshotted.

title: Data: MCR read model — RevisionStore.getRevisionByTitle/getById/getKnownLatestRevision + return type
description: IN: the end-to-end 'latest/any revision of a title' read — page-conds + rev_id=page_latest join; actor + comment resolution in the revision query; slots+content join; role/model name resolution via ws2-s6; lazy blob via ws2-s7; WAN row-cache for current revision; empty-slots primary fallback (T212428); missing-main-slot exception; rev_deleted audience filtering. Define the MCR read-model RETURN TYPE (RevisionRecord-equivalent: id/page/parent/timestamp/actor/comment/len/sha1 + getSlots()/getContent(role,audience)). OUT: revision INSERT + CAS (WS5); RevisionRenderer/ParserOutput (WS3); archive/undelete.
design: Verified: RevisionStore::getRevisionByTitle/getRevisionById/getKnownLatestRevision/newRevisionFromRow(AndSlots)/loadSlotRecords/constructSlotRecords/getQueryInfo/getSlotsQueryInfo. Actor join + CommentStore join always present; role/model resolved in-memory via NameTableStore. getKnownLatestRevision WAN TTL_WEEK keyed (domain,pageId,revId). This RETURN TYPE is the primary input to WS3 (read render) and WS4 (revision endpoints).
acceptance_criteria: BYTE-PARITY of resolved main-slot content + revision metadata vs PHP RevisionStore across a fixture set (single-slot, multi-slot, inherited-slot, rev_deleted under FOR_PUBLIC/RAW); identical (actor_name, comment_text, sha1, len) per fixture.
notes: Test: integration against a DB seeded from a real MediaWiki install/dump; cross-check each field vs PHP. Multi-slot + inherited-slot fixtures required. (Blocked by ws2-s1, ws2-s4, ws2-s6, ws2-s7.)

title: Data: TS NameTableStore (read + 3-tier cache) for slot_roles / content_models
description: IN: getId(name)/getName(id)/getMap() with in-process -> WAN-global-key -> replica-full-scan caching; per-table normalization; getName primary fallback for unknown id; getId throw-on-miss; global cache key (NameTableSqlStore, table, domain). OUT: acquireId/store/WAN-purge/transaction-volatility (WS5); change_tag_def (WS6 change-tags).
design: Fully verified: includes/Storage/NameTableStore.php + NameTableStoreFactory.php. NORMALIZATION ASYMMETRY (load-bearing, silent-bug risk): slot_roles uses normalizationCallback=strtolower; content_models uses NONE (deliberate — mixed-case model names). A port that normalizes both, or neither, mis-resolves IDs. Used by constructSlotRecords to resolve role_name/model_name in-memory.
acceptance_criteria: Resolves 'main'->role id and 'wikitext'->model id against the seeded DB; case-INsensitive role lookup, case-SENSITIVE model lookup; unknown role-name id throws; cache populated once then served in-process.
notes: Test: unit on cache tiers with fake cache+db; integration against seeded slot_roles/content_models. (Blocked by ws2-s3.)

title: Data: TS connection provider (replica/primary split, query groups, domains)
description: IN: an IConnectionProvider-shaped TS interface — getReplicaDatabase(domain?,group?)->IReadableDatabase, getPrimaryDatabase(domain?)->IDatabase; read/write split enforced at the type level (no write methods on the read handle); READ_NORMAL/READ_LATEST/READ_LOCKING recency flags routing reads to replica vs primary; query-group hint + domain (dbname,schema,prefix) plumbing. OUT: transaction rounds, DBO_TRX, ChronologyProtector (ws2-s5), LoadMonitor weighting, write builders (WS5).
design: Interface: includes/libs/rdbms/LBFactory/IConnectionProvider.php (since 1.40). Flag routing verified in RevisionStore::getDBConnectionRefForQueryFlags (READ_LATEST->primary else replica). Constants DB_PRIMARY=-2/DB_REPLICA=-1 (LoadBalancer). CORRECTION: the PHP code is mid-migration ILoadBalancer->IConnectionProvider (RevisionStore/NameTableStore still take ILoadBalancer with '// TODO: Replace with ICP') — target the ICP narrow interface as the store-facing contract, not the legacy LoadBalancer surface.
acceptance_criteria: Read handle is compile-time write-incapable; READ_LATEST routes to primary; the same (server,domain) ref is reused (lazy connect); against a live MySQL fixture DB the provider returns working replica + primary handles.
notes: Test: unit on routing with a fake driver; integration against containerized MySQL seeded from tables-generated.sql. Open Q: how much LoadBalancer (weighted replica pick) to port now vs single-replica stub.

title: Data: fluent SelectQueryBuilder (read subset) + Expression over the TS driver
description: IN: newSelectQueryBuilder() with select/from/where/andWhere/join(LEFT JOIN)/orderBy/limit/caller/fetchRow/fetchResultSet/fetchField; expr() type-safe conditions; table-prefix + value-quoting; forUpdate() under READ_LOCKING; single-use semantics; fluent extensibility (RevisionSelectQueryBuilder adds joinComment/joinPage/joinUser). OUT: Insert/Update/Delete/Replace/Union builders (WS5).
design: Canonical pattern verified in docs/database.md and used throughout RevisionStore/NameTableStore/SqlBlobStore. RevisionSelectQueryBuilder extends the base with joinComment/joinPage/joinUser — the TS builder must support the same fluent extension. forUpdate path in fetchRevisionRowFromConds. Must express the rev_id=page_latest + page-conds query and the slots+content join.
acceptance_criteria: Builds the exact rev_id=page_latest + page-conds query and the slots+content join; emitted SQL matches the PHP shape (modulo quoting); rejects reuse of a spent builder.
notes: Test: unit SQL-string assertions (mirror the rdbms QueryBuilder unit tests); integration fetch against the seeded DB. (Blocked by ws2-s3.)

title: Data: TS DDL generator + parity gate vs PHP tables-generated.sql (MySQL/Postgres/SQLite)
description: IN: emit per-dialect CREATE TABLE/index DDL for MySQL, Postgres, SQLite from the ws2-s1 model; reproduce dialect quirks; a parity test that format-normalizes (mirroring Doctrine SqlFormatter) and diffs against the committed sql/{mysql,postgres,sqlite}/tables-generated.sql. OUT: applying DDL / installer / update.php; schema-change patches.
design: CORRECTION vs Epic: the AbstractSchemaTest gate is FORMAT-NORMALIZED, not byte-exact (assertSQLSame runs both sides through SqlFormatter) — reproduce tokens/ordering/dialect quirks, not literal whitespace. Concrete quirks (verified in the generated SQL): Postgres DROPS UNSIGNED; MySQL carries /*_*/ table-prefix placeholders + /*$wgDBTableOptions*/; mw* types need the MediaWiki SchemaGenerator custom-type layer (mwtimestamp/mwenum/mwtinyint) — a naive Doctrine passthrough will not reproduce these.
acceptance_criteria: TS-generated DDL for page/revision/slots/content/content_models/text/comment/actor format-normalize-equals the PHP-generated SQL for all three dialects.
notes: Test: snapshot/diff harness over the committed tables-generated.sql; per-dialect cases. Open Q: how many of the 64 tables to gate in the proving slice vs full. (Blocked by ws2-s1.)

title: Data: TS row-type + abstract-schema model generated from sql/tables.json
description: IN: parse sql/tables.json; emit TS interfaces for every table column (page, revision, slots, slot_roles, content, content_models, text, comment, actor at minimum) with faithful type/nullability/unsigned mapping; map the abstract type enum (incl. mwtimestamp/mwenum/mwtinyint) to TS representations; preserve the role_id(int) vs slot_role_id(smallint-unsigned) asymmetry; validate input against docs/abstract-schema-table.json. OUT: DDL/SQL emission (ws2-s2); migrations; runtime queries.
design: Source enum verified at docs/abstract-schema-table.json::type. Column structure in sql/tables.json (columns[].options: notnull/unsigned/length/autoincrement/PlatformOptions). mwtimestamp is a 14-char binary on MySQL -> model as a branded string, not Date. WIDTH ASYMMETRY TRAP: slot_roles.role_id & content_models.model_id are signed integer, but slots.slot_role_id & content.content_model are smallint unsigned — mirror exactly, do not normalize both sides.
acceptance_criteria: Generated TS types cover all 64 tables; spot-fixtures assert slots.slot_role_id=unsigned smallint and slot_roles.role_id=signed integer; round-trips a known revision fixture row without loss.
notes: bd-run: implemented but unverified (20260615-132803); needs human review; see .bd-run-logs/mw-9pd.10-20260615-132803.log

title: Runtime: resident-process model — boot-once bootstrap, request isolation wiring, graceful lifecycle
description: IN: the resident Node process model — build the container + frozen config ONCE at process start (boot-per-request -> boot-once), then serve N requests each with isolated context (ws1-s2) + deferred queue (ws1-s5); the worker model (cluster/worker_threads decision); graceful shutdown/drain; per-request crash isolation (an unhandled error in one request must not corrupt the process or another request). OUT: container internals (ws1-s1), config internals (ws1-s3), context internals (ws1-s2), deferred internals (ws1-s5) — this composes them into the running server.
design: The heart of the Epic's 'real re-architecture'. PHP's shared-nothing crash isolation (handbook ch.09) must be re-EARNED in a resident loop via per-request context isolation, no shared mutable module state, and bounded worker recycling (the resident analog of opcache+restart). Eliminate process-global mutable singletons: RequestContext::$instance, Profiler per-request data, LoggerFactory context, DeferredUpdates::$scopeStack must all become request-local; MediaWikiServices::$instance is process-scoped by design. resetGlobalInstance's 'DATA LOSS' warnings are PHP test-only; the container is immutable post-boot in serving.
acceptance_criteria: Process boots container+config once (factory/load called once across many requests); an exception deep in one request returns an error response and leaves the process + a concurrent request unaffected; graceful shutdown drains in-flight requests + POSTSEND work before exit.
notes: Test: integration load/chaos test — boot once, fire concurrent requests incl. a poisoned one, assert isolation + single boot + clean drain; no PHP analog (this is the divergence point). Open Q: worker recycling policy; cluster vs worker_threads vs single-process+AsyncLocalStorage (depends on ws1-s2).

title: Runtime: config system — load config-schema.php/YAML as data into a typed Config + ServiceOptions
description: IN: a SettingsBuilder-equivalent that loads the schema AS DATA (port includes/config-schema.php -> JSON/TS, or consume docs/config-schema.yaml), overlays site config, applies merge strategies + dynamicDefault callbacks, then freezes (loading->registration->read-only); a Config read interface (get/has) and ServiceOptions (frozen narrow snapshot, exact-match assertRequiredOptions); generate TS name constants (the MainConfigNames equivalent). OUT: the 767 settings' meanings (each subsystem owns its own); LocalSettings.php PHP-execution compat (defer to WS7); the $wg* global bridge (greenfield drops globals).
design: includes/config-schema.php is already pure data (return [...]) -> directly portable. MainConfigSchema.php = 767 public const settings (single source of truth) with default/type/mergeStrategy/deprecated/dynamicDefault. The 3-stage SettingsBuilder lifecycle (Setup.php:234 enterRegistrationStage, :294 enterReadOnlyStage) maps to a builder that freezes once at process start. ServiceOptions exact-match (fails on missing OR extra key) documents per-service config deps — preserve it. Merge strategies (array_plus, array_plus_2d, array_replace_recursive, provide_default) must be ported faithfully (list vs map typing is load-bearing; 'array' is banned).
acceptance_criteria: Schema loads from a data file; Config.get('Sitename') returns default 'MediaWiki'; site override wins with the correct merge strategy; ServiceOptions throws on extra OR missing key; config is immutable after freeze (mutation throws).
notes: Test: port ServiceOptionsTest, SettingsBuilderTest, HashConfigTest semantics; fixture = a small schema subset + an override file. Open Q: YAML vs PHP-array-as-JSON as the canonical TS schema source.

title: Runtime: per-request context object + request-isolation model (replace RequestContext::getMain singleton)
description: IN: a RequestContext-equivalent value object (request, response, authority/title placeholders, language, output sink, timing) that is PER-REQUEST, explicitly passed, never a process singleton; the request/response abstraction; the isolation boundary (what is per-request vs per-process in a resident loop); the async-context propagation mechanism. OUT: Authority/Title semantics (WS6/WS3), actual output rendering (WS3) — this provides typed slots for them.
design: RequestContext::getMain() (includes/context/RequestContext.php:109,615) is the god-singleton threaded everywhere — the single biggest re-architecture point. Enumerate process-global state that must become request-local: RequestContext::$instance, Profiler per-request data, DeferredUpdates::$scopeStack, LoggerFactory context. REST uses a SEPARATE RequestInterface (includes/Rest/EntryPoint.php:155) distinct from the WebRequest inside RequestContext — the abstraction must allow a distinct request type per handler family. Decide Node AsyncLocalStorage vs explicit threading (constrains every downstream handler signature).
acceptance_criteria: Two concurrent simulated requests see fully isolated context (no field bleed); no context reachable via a module-level singleton; handler signature receives context explicitly. Verified by a concurrency test interleaving two requests.
notes: Test: new concurrency unit test (two requests in flight, assert isolation); model against the RequestContext field set. Open Q: AsyncLocalStorage vs explicit threading.

title: Runtime: TS service container (DI engine) with lazy singletons, manipulators, reset/destroy
description: IN: port ServiceContainer semantics to TS — defineService/getService (lazy, cached, loop-detected), has/peek, redefineService, addServiceManipulator, destroy()/salvage(), DestructibleService/SalvageableService contracts; a MediaWikiServices-equivalent root container with a strongly-typed service-token registry (TS generics, not 245 hand-written getters); container built from a declarative wiring module. OUT: the actual service factories (each workstream owns its own); config loading (ws1-s3); hook firing in the container (ws1-s4).
design: Mirror vendor/wikimedia/services/src/ServiceContainer.php ($serviceInstantiators, $serviceManipulators, $servicesBeingCreated loop guard). MediaWikiServices extends ServiceContainer adding the bootstrap lifecycle (allowGlobalInstance, resetGlobalInstance, salvage, disableStorage). Scale to replace: ServiceWiring.php=256 factory closures, MediaWikiServices=245 typed getters -> collapse to container.get(Token). In a resident model the container is built once at process start, so salvage/reset likely collapse to 'build once, never reset in serving path' (verify against failIfResetNotAllowed).
acceptance_criteria: Container resolves a registered factory exactly once (factory call count==1 across N gets); circular dependency throws with the dependency chain; unknown service throws NoSuchService; a manipulator runs after the factory; destroy() calls destroy() on DestructibleServices and makes further get() throw.
notes: Test: port ServiceContainerTest + the MediaWikiServicesTest round-trip invariant (every token resolves to its declared type); unit-level, no fixtures. Open Q: keep salvage/reset or assert no-reset-in-serving-path (resolve with ws1-s7).

title: Epic: Reimplement MediaWiki core as a TypeScript/Node engine (greenfield, data-compatible)
description:
Reimplement MediaWiki core as a TypeScript/Node engine (greenfield, data-compatible).

A TS/Node engine serves what index.php / api.php / rest.php serve today, running
against the EXISTING MediaWiki database schema, with PHP core retired and a single
PHP Parsoid sidecar retained for wikitext. Pursued as a multi-year incremental
strangler (read paths -> writes -> retire PHP), NOT a translation of the PHP.

Greenfield: the in-process PHP extension/skin ecosystem (VisualEditor, Wikibase,
CirrusSearch, all skins) is OUT of scope; this is a permanent fork. Enabled by the
language-agnostic abstract schema (sql/tables.json) and by reusing PHP Parsoid as
a network sidecar (removes the parser rewrite from the critical path).

Epic plan: docs/epics/nodejs-migration.md
Breakdown companion: docs/epics/nodejs-migration-breakdown.md (this breakdown)

Confidence: medium. Live uncertainties = write-path data-compat correctness,
the Parsoid-over-network DataAccess contract, and the multi-year runway.

title: Track Beads issues in source
description: Make the current Beads issue set available through Git-tracked project files so other developers can import or inspect it instead of relying on a single local embedded Dolt checkout.
acceptance_criteria: Portable Beads metadata and a JSONL export of current issues are tracked in source; local Dolt/runtime files remain ignored; README explains how developers refresh or import the issue snapshot.
close_reason: Committed portable Beads metadata and JSONL issue snapshot to source tracking.

title: Cutover: NEAR-TERM — API wire-parity harness (Action + REST contract diff)
description: IN: point the existing tests/api-testing/ specs (or a thin parity wrapper) at both the PHP wiki and the TS engine (WS4 endpoints) and diff responses; lean on the built-in OpenAPI oracle for REST (satisfyApiSpec via /specs/v0/module/-) so TS REST responses validate against the same contract; diff JSON shape for a curated set of action.* specs. OUT: HTML body render-fidelity (ws7-s1); dual-write; routing.
design: api-testing v1.7.1 Mocha framework; REST=new REST('rest.php') and action.* clients (tests/api-testing/REST/PageHistory.js, action/Parse.js). OpenAPI runtime validation confirmed (PageHistory.js:120-143). Complements the in-process structure tests (RestStructureTest, ApiStructureTest, ApiPrefixUniquenessTest, SpecialPageFatalTest) — port their equivalents to TS so the harness isn't the only contract net. Note Transform.js is mostly skipForNow (T283875) — audit before reuse. Consumes WS4 endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: The same api-testing spec runs green vs the PHP wiki and reports a structured diff vs the TS engine; TS REST responses pass to.satisfyApiSpec against the live OpenAPI; a curated Action-API set produces a pass/diff report; base-URI is parameterized (PHP vs TS) without forking the specs.
notes: Test: run the suite vs PHP as control, then vs a stub TS endpoint to prove diff detection; verify OpenAPI validation rejects a malformed TS response. (Blocked by ws4-s3.) Open Q: which Action modules are in-scope; re-enable the skipped Transform.js cases.

title: Cutover: NEAR-TERM — engine-aware read-path parity harness (TS-Parsoid vs PHP-Parsoid)
description: IN: a harness that renders a wikitext input via the TS engine (WS3 read render) and via PHP, and diffs the HTML; drive it from tests/parser/*.txt reading the html/parsoid section as the oracle (NOT html/php); DOM-normalize before compare (normalize data-parsoid offsets to the agreed tolerance); emit a per-case pass/fail/diff report + an aggregate parity-rate; reuse the ParserTestRunner fixture-parsing logic. This is the WS3 enabler AND the artifact WS7 cutover consumes. OUT: any write path; HTTP/wire concerns (ws7-s2); traffic routing; legacy html/php comparison (wrong oracle for the Parsoid slice).
design: CORRECTION vs Epic: parser-test fixtures are a clean oracle ONLY for legacy-Parser output. The proving slice is Parsoid-routed, and html/parsoid is annotation-laden DOM (data-parsoid/data-mw/typeof), NOT html/php. Per handbook ch.10 decision #6 the two engines 'diverge in HTML output by design' — comparing against html/php would report thousands of false failures. Fixtures: tests/parser/parserTests.txt (22 of 29 files carry html/parsoid; 697 sections). Runner to reuse: MediaWiki\Tests\Common\Parser\ParserTestRunner.
acceptance_criteria: Running the harness over a fixture file produces a deterministic parity-rate + per-case diff list; a deliberately-divergent TS render is flagged, an identical render passes; it selects html/parsoid + applies the agreed DOM normalization (a fixture differing only in data-parsoid offsets passes); runnable headless in CI in fixture-oracle mode with no running wiki.
notes: Test: self-test with crafted matching/mismatching pairs; run across a sample fixture file; golden-test the diff format. (Blocked by ws3-s3.) Open Q: DOM-normalization tolerance (exact vs normalized); add a live-PHP-wiki oracle mode for non-corpus inputs.

title: Write: SPIKE — write-path data-compat invariants + golden-fixture corpus (do first)
description: IN: produce an executable invariant spec + golden-fixture corpus from the running PHP engine — byte-exact algorithms for content_sha1 (base36/sha1/pad-31 over serialized bytes), rev_sha1 (role-NAME sort + left-fold), comment_hash (crc32 XOR + signed-32 fold + visual truncation + FormatJson ALL_OK), slot_origin inheritance, blob old_flags/address format, actor actor_name normalization, page_props encodeValue; the FULL table-touch inventory per edit (atomic vs deferred vs job) and the non-idempotent counter list; the event-driven dispatch contract; cross-engine round-trip fixtures. This feeds the WS1 runtime decision and WS2/WS7.
design: All citations below. Key primitive: base36Sha1(x)=leftPad(base36(sha1hex(x)),31,'0') (SlotRecord.php:615). comment_hash null-data term = crc32('')=0 (CommentStore.php:380). rev_sha1 sorts slots by role NAME (RevisionSlots::computeSha1:181) but findIdenticalRevision sorts by role ID (RevisionStore.php:3387) — do not conflate. NameTable/actor IDs are DB-allocated, never predicted.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture suite where, for a representative corpus (new page, edit, null edit, dummy rev, multi-slot, rollback/inherited slot, anon-IP edit, structured-comment edit), TS-computed content_sha1/rev_sha1/comment_hash/old_flags/slot_origin match the PHP-produced DB rows byte-for-byte; document reviewable by WS1/WS2/WS7.
notes: Test: generate fixtures from rows the PHP engine actually wrote; assert TS pure functions reproduce them; property tests on the hash folds. MILESTONE+SPIKE. No blocking dependency — this is the early unblocker; land before WS1/WS2 finalize their runtime/DBAL designs.

title: API: resources/ coupling audit + mw.Api/mw.Rest reuse plan (Handoff #5)
description: IN: the authoritative reuse decision — inventory (a) pure-JSON consumers (mediawiki.api/ incl. rest.js/mw.Rest, ForeignApi) = reusable; (b) PHP-rendered-output dependents (startup.js RLCONF/RLPAGEMODULES bootstrap, ~95 mw.config.get callers, ~11 server-rendered-DOM readers, mediawiki.action*) = blocked on WS3; define the RLCONF/RLPAGEMODULES contract the TS OutputPage-equivalent must emit (handed to WS3); verify mw.Rest default URL (mw.util.wikiScript('rest')) resolves on the TS backend. OUT: re-implementing OutputPage/Skin or the RLCONF bootstrap (WS3); changing resources/ source.
design: CORRECTION vs Epic (Handoff #5): the 'resources/ largely reusable' assumption is HALF true. Reusable as-is against JSON: resources/src/mediawiki.api/ + rest.js (pure HTTP-JSON clients). NOT reusable: resources/src/startup/startup.js:123-125 bootstraps the whole front end from window.RLCONF/RLSTATE/RLPAGEMODULES — inline <script> emitted by PHP OutputPage/Skin (OutputPage.php getJsConfigVars + getRlClient()->getHeadHtml()), not any API. So the in-wiki UI cannot run on TS APIs alone until WS3 re-implements the bootstrap+skin. This decision/seam is OWNED BY WS3, not WS4.
acceptance_criteria: A documented two-tier classification with file counts; a named RLCONF/RLPAGEMODULES contract handed to WS3; a list of resources/ modules confirmed reusable against TS JSON unchanged.
notes: Test: manual reachability audit + a smoke test pointing mw.Api/mw.Rest at the TS backend for one read call. (Blocked by ws4-s3; FEEDS WS3 ws3-s5.) Open Q: will WS3 server-render skin HTML in TS or pivot to a client-rendered shell (changes the blocked-tier size dramatically).

title: API: first REST read endpoints — page source + bare + page HTML
description: IN: one vertical per endpoint (route + handler + output-shape conformance + contract test) for GET /v1/page/{title}, /v1/page/{title}/bare (PageSourceHandler) and GET /v1/page/{title}/html (PageHTMLHandler); the PageContentHelper (source/metadata) + consuming WS3's HtmlOutputRendererHelper for the HTML variant; needsWriteAccess()=false, ETag/Last-Modified, redirect-normalization, 404-on-nonexistent. OUT: transform/Parsoid write-back endpoints; revision-range/history (ws4-s6); RESTBase output mode.
design: Rest/Handler/PageSourceHandler.php (run() switches bare/source; body shape = Schema/ExistingPageSource.json + ExistingPageBare.json — the exact contract: id,key,title,latest{id,timestamp},content_model,license,source/html_url). Rest/Handler/PageHTMLHandler.php (htmlHelper->getHtml() returns a ParserOutput-equivalent — WS3 read render artifact). Rest/Handler/Helper/PageContentHelper.php consumes RevisionLookup/PageLookup — WS2 read artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: Response body byte-matches PHP REST output for a fixture title for /page/{title}, /bare, /html; required fields per the schema files; correct ETag/Cache-Control; 404 with rest-nonexistent-title for a missing page; matches tests/api-testing/REST/PageLegacy.js.
notes: Test: port/run tests/api-testing/REST/PageLegacy.js against the TS server; golden-fixture diff vs the response schemas. (Blocked by ws4-s1, ws2-s8, ws3-s3.) Open Q: exact ParserOutput-equivalent surface WS3 exposes for /html.

title: Read: TS server-side skinning — one Mustache skin + RL link assembly + same-URL serving
description: IN: assemble the final HTML document for the constrained set using ONE skin (e.g. the fallback Mustache template) over a getTemplateData()-equivalent; emit RL <link>/<script> bootstrap (head, frozen after body); serve behind the SAME URL contract as PHP (the canonical view URL). OUT: multiple skins, ResourceLoader load.php module delivery (reuse the existing PHP load.php — client JS is reusable), authenticated views, editing chrome.
design: CONFIRMED vs Epic: skins are PHP/Mustache (includes/Skin/SkinMustache.php renders .mustache via TemplateParser; templates in resources/templates/skins/) — server-side skinning IS a rewrite. Mirror Skin::outputPageFinal order (includes/Skin/Skin.php:678): body first, then headElement (OutputPage.php:3871, freezes the RL queue), then tailElement. The inline RLCONF + startup <script async src=load.php?modules=startup> must match so the existing PHP load.php serves the modules. (Consumes the RLCONF/RLPAGEMODULES contract from ws4-s4.)
acceptance_criteria: Full-page HTML for an anonymous view of a constrained page is structurally equivalent to PHP's (same skin, same RL bootstrap, browser loads modules from the existing load.php); served at the identical URL. Certified by the ws7-s1 parity harness.
notes: Test: DOM-normalized full-page compare vs PHP output; smoke test that the served page loads RL modules against the real load.php. (Blocked by ws3-s4.) Open Q: which mw.config vars are required early vs late.

title: Read: TS read render — Title -> revision -> Parsoid render -> ParserOutput-equivalent + ParserCache
description: IN: resolve Title for the constrained set, fetch the current revision (WS2 MCR read), call the sidecar (ws3-s2) for a page-bundle, materialize a ParserOutput-equivalent, and store/retrieve from a TS Parsoid ParserCache-equivalent keyed like ParserCache::makeParserOutputKey (page id + options hash) in a parsoid-* keyspace. OUT: OutputTransform (ws3-s4), skinning (ws3-s5), write-side cache invalidation (WS5), old-revision cache.
design: Mirror ParserOutputAccess::getCachedParserOutput/getParserOutput (includes/Page/ParserOutputAccess.php:305,440) and the Parsoid cache names (PARSOID_PCACHE_NAME, :50). CORRECTION vs Epic: there are TWO ParserCaches with a Parsoid-specific keyspace (parsoid-parser/parsoid-rparser) — the TS cache must be a separate keyspace. Title resolution needs LinkCache/LinkBatch (includes/Page/LinkCache.php, LinkBatch.php) — batch existence once. Skip makeLimitReport/linting on the proof (they pull the legacy parser). The read path is NOT purely read-only in PHP (linting writes, metadata) — suppress those on the slice.
acceptance_criteria: For each constrained page, the TS pre-transform HTML byte-matches the PHP Parsoid cache entry (html/parsoid fixture parity); a second request is a cache hit (no sidecar call); the cache key matches core's algorithm for the same options.
notes: Test: parser-test-fixture parity on html/parsoid sections; cache hit/miss assertions; key-format unit test vs makeParserOutputKey. (Blocked by ws3-s2, ws2-s8, ws1-s2.) Open Q: which ParserOptions participate in the key for the constrained set (mostly default -> canonical).

title: Read: TS OutputTransform pipeline (DOM path) for Parsoid output
description: IN: port the ordered post-cache pipeline for the Parsoid/DOM path needed by the constrained set — ExtractBody, AddWrapperDivClass (mw-parser-output), HandleParsoidSectionLinks, HandleTOCMarkersDOM, DeduplicateStylesDOM, ExpandToAbsoluteUrlsDOM, HardenNFC (last); add ParsoidLanguageConverter/ParsoidLocalization only if the constrained set's language requires them. OUT: Text-variant stages (legacy parser only), hook-execution stages, debug/limit-report rendering.
design: OutputTransformPipeline::run (includes/OutputTransform/OutputTransformPipeline.php:61) clones the ParserOutput then runs stages gated by shouldRun(). Ordering in DefaultOutputPipelineFactory::CORE_LIST is load-bearing (lang convert before section links/TOC; HardenNFC always last). Stage classes live in includes/OutputTransform/Stages/. Note: stages exist in DOM and Text variants — Parsoid output takes the DOM path.
acceptance_criteria: Transformed HTML byte-matches PHP's post-transform output for the constrained set (what addPostProcessedParserOutput would emit, minus skin chrome).
notes: Test: golden-HTML compare vs PHP post-transform output; per-stage unit tests. (Blocked by ws3-s3.) Open Q: whether section-edit-link injection is in scope for anonymous views (likely off).

title: Data: TS SqlBlobStore read path (address resolution + decompress)
description: IN: getBlob(address)/getBlobBatch(); splitBlobAddress() contract (schema:id?params, lowercased schema); tt:->text.old_id fetch (old_text/old_flags); decompress per old_flags (gzip/utf-8/object); WAN cache by address (immutable, no negative caching); surface BadBlobException/BlobAccessException on corruption. OUT: blob WRITING/compression (WS5); deep ExternalStore (es:) cluster routing (stub/throw OK for the proving slice).
design: Verified: includes/Storage/SqlBlobStore.php (getBlob, fetchBlobs, expandBlob, decompressData, splitBlobAddress, makeAddressFromTextId). No negative caching is deliberate (corrupt-replica safety). Blobs are read replica-first because text is immutable.
acceptance_criteria: Resolves a tt:NNN address to decompressed bytes matching the PHP store for a fixture row; a malformed address throws; es: returns a clear not-yet-implemented error.
notes: Test: unit on address split + decompress with fixtures; integration against seeded text. (Blocked by ws2-s3.)

title: Data: ChronologyProtector read-side (read-your-writes wait)
description: IN: a getSessionPrimaryPos-equivalent — read the saved primary position from a DC-local cpStash by clientId; before replica reads, wait (bounded) for the chosen replica to reach that position; enter lagged mode (shortened cache-TTL signal) on timeout; disabled in CLI. OUT: write-side staging/persistence, clientId/cookie minting, position marshalling (WS5).
design: Read role + storage in includes/libs/rdbms/ChronologyProtector.php (class docblock; getSessionPrimaryPos). cpStash = low-latency, DC-local, non-durable, no replication. Shares the write-side contract (cpStash key format + position marshalling) with WS5 (ws5-s7) — agree it early. Read-side can ship and be unit-tested standalone against a fake stash.
acceptance_criteria: Given a staged position, the provider waits until the replica catches up before the first read; on timeout it proceeds in lagged mode without erroring; CLI bypasses entirely.
notes: Test: unit with a fake stash + fake replica position; integration deferred (needs a replication topology). (Blocked by ws2-s3; shares contract with ws5-s7.)

title: Runtime: entry-point handler framework — base lifecycle + the 6 web handlers + CLI seam
description: IN: a TS MediaWikiEntryPoint-equivalent base (setup->execute->prepareForOutput->postOutputShutdown) with a top-level Throwable->error-renderer catch; the URL/SAPI router; skeleton handler classes (execute() bodies delegated to owning workstreams) for the 6 real web handlers (Action/index, Api, Rest, ResourceLoader/load, Thumbnail, AuthenticatedFile) + the opensearch_desc 308-redirect ROUTE; a maintenance/CLI entry seam; per-handler error format (HTML / API / REST JSON). OUT: handler execute() business logic (WS3/WS4/WS6); the deferred/output machinery (ws1-s5).
design: MediaWikiEntryPoint::run() (:176) is the template (setup/execute/prepareForOutput/postOutputShutdown). CORRECTION vs Epic: opensearch_desc.php is NOT a handler — it's a plain 308 redirect to /rest/v1/search (max-age=600), so it's a router rule (net = 6 web handlers + CLI, not 7+1). REST has a 4-arg constructor (separate RequestInterface). EntryPointEnvironment (isCli/hasFastCgi/exit) is a PHP-runtime shim; in Node most of it (FastCGI, ob_*) is moot — port only isCli/env/exit.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the 6 handlers is constructable and run()-able with a stub execute(); an uncaught error in execute() routes to the handler's error renderer with the right content-type; the opensearch_desc route returns 308 to the search REST path with max-age=600.
notes: Test: integration smoke test per entry point (stub execute, assert lifecycle + error path); reuse the request/response fixtures from ws1-s2. Open Q: single Node HTTP server + router vs per-entry-point processes (resident model favors one server).

title: Runtime: internal lifecycle-event seam (minimal hook replacement; extension dispatch dropped)
description: IN: a minimal typed internal event/callback mechanism replacing only core's self-fired boot/lifecycle hooks (onSetupAfterCache, onMediaWikiServices) + a decision record on whether Domain Events survive as the post-commit notification primitive. Document that the full HookContainer/HookRunner/extension.json/ExtensionRegistry/ExtensionProcessor surface is REMOVED. OUT: extension.json parsing, $wgHooks merge ordering, the ~540 hook interfaces — all dropped.
design: CORRECTION vs Epic: the hook system canNOT be fully dropped. Core fires hooks on itself: Setup.php:476 onSetupAfterCache; MediaWikiServices.php:375,467 onMediaWikiServices. The Domain Event system (includes/DomainEvent/, EventDispatchEngine) is implemented on top of HookContainer+DeferredUpdates, so events double as hook names. Accurate scope = 'drop the dispatcher + extension.json, keep a minimal internal lifecycle-callback seam'. If Domain Events survive they ride ws1-s5's deferred model, coordinated with WS5.
acceptance_criteria: Boot completes with a documented lifecycle-callback seam; no general-purpose hook dispatcher exists; a registered boot-complete callback fires once after container init (boot integration test).
notes: Test: boot integration test asserting callback ordering vs container readiness. Open Q (cross WS5): keep/drop/replace Domain Events — this story records the decision.

title: Runtime: deferred-work model for the resident runtime (PRESEND/POSTSEND redesign)
description: IN: redesign DeferredUpdates for a resident event loop — a per-request deferred-work queue with PRESEND (complete before response flush) and POSTSEND (after response sent) semantics, scoped to the request (no process-global $scopeStack); MergeableUpdate batching; EnqueueableDataUpdate->job fallback; the 'no retry for plain deferred' guarantee; how POSTSEND runs in Node. OUT: the job-queue backend (WS5/WS6); ChronologyProtector correctness (WS2/WS5); transaction-round semantics (WS2).
design: includes/Deferred/DeferredUpdates.php constants ALL/PRESEND(1)/POSTSEND(2), default POSTSEND; lifecycle in MediaWikiEntryPoint::commitMainTransaction (PRESEND, :281) + restInPeace (POSTSEND, :652). KEY GREENFIELD WIN: ~400 lines of MediaWikiEntryPoint (fastcgi_finish_request, Content-Length/Connection-close tricks, ob_* wrappers) exist ONLY to fake async-after-response in PHP; Node does this natively — do NOT port them (flag so reviewers don't 'restore parity'). Scope stack must become request-local (ties ws1-s2). CLI collapses PRESEND/POSTSEND.
acceptance_criteria: PRESEND updates complete before response bytes are sent; POSTSEND updates run after the client has the full response and don't block it; MergeableUpdates coalesce; a failed EnqueueableDataUpdate falls back to enqueue; two requests' deferred queues don't interleave.
notes: Test: unit+integration on ordering and isolation; model against the DeferredUpdates docblock flow. Open Q: where the ChronologyProtector cookie writes live (surface the hook points; WS2/WS5 own correctness).

title: Build bd-pipeline: Python multi-model Claude orchestrator (plan/implement/review/fix loop) in wiseblox-assembly
description: Standalone Python CLI replacing scripts/bd-run.sh with a per-issue pipeline: Plan (opus max) -> Implement (sonnet high) -> Review (opus max, fresh adversarial) <-> Fix (sonnet high, resumes implement session) until review passes -> commit + close. Lives in /Users/todorpetrov/GitHub/wiseblox/wiseblox-assembly. Ports bd-run.sh gating + commit-only-touched logic and factory's run_cli seam. Plan: ~/.claude/plans/lively-fluttering-sprout.md
notes: Built in /Users/todorpetrov/GitHub/wiseblox/wiseblox-assembly (13 modules + 9 test files, 51 unittests green, zero runtime deps). Pipeline: Plan(opus/max,read-only)->Implement(sonnet/high,bypass)->Review(opus/max,fresh)<->Fix(sonnet/high,resume impl)->commit-only-touched+close. Validated --list/--dry-run against live bd (gates spikes .18/.30, clears .12/.4/.3/.2). NOT yet run live (autonomous agent spawn needs user go). Install needs a venv (Homebrew python is PEP668 externally-managed).

title: Build bd-run.sh agent driver loop (bd ready → claude -p → verify → close)
description: A thin headless-Claude driver that drains the bd ready queue and implements issues autonomously, with risk-class gating so decision-gated issues (spikes, cutover gates, incremental-counter stories) are skipped for human handling. Implements option (b) from the node-engine implementation strategy discussion: keeps the bd dependency graph and parity gates in the loop, which the GitHub-shaped OSS runners (OpenHands, Claude Code Action) would lose.
notes:
Built scripts/bd-run.sh. Validated: bash -n, --list, --dry-run --all, prompt rendering, risk-class gating (spikes .18/.30 skip on 'spike' label; .35 on 'decision-gated'; .46/.47/.48 on 'Cutover: MILESTONE'; .44/.45 parity harnesses NOT gated). Log dir added to .gitignore. NOT yet run live: the harness gates spawning a nested acceptEdits agent (correct) — needs explicit user go for first real run.
Superseded by mw-pcr (Python bd-pipeline): same gating + commit-only-touched logic, plus the plan/implement/review/fix multi-model loop. scripts/bd-run.sh remains as the simple single-call driver.

title: Breadth: MILESTONE — localisation / i18n engine (LCStore-equivalent)
description: IN: reuse languages/i18n/*.json verbatim as data; reimplement Message resolution (formats + escaping boundary), LocalisationCache compile/merge/fallback with a pluggable store equivalent, MessageCache on-wiki override layer, LanguageFallback chains, plural/gender/grammar, number/date/directionality formatting, and translation of MessagesXx.php structural config + the LanguageXx quirk subclasses. OUT: LanguageConverter (script-variant zh/sr — defer), the translatewiki.net sync tooling.
design: CORRECTION vs Epic: 'reuse the message JSON' is true+cheap (i18n/*.json is a clean key->value map, portable verbatim), but 'reuse localisation' is a real reimplementation — MessagesXx.php is executable PHP config ($fallback/$namespaceNames/$magicWords/$specialPageAliases), ~33 LanguageXx subclasses encode plural/grammar rules data can't express, and plural rules come from CLDR XML (languages/data/plurals.xml). LocalisationCache.php resolves LCStore via getStoreFromConf (files->CDB, db->DB, array->StaticArray). Escaping (->text/->escaped/->parse/->plain) is a security boundary.
acceptance_criteria: A known set of en/de/zh-hans messages resolve through the fallback chain with correct plural/gender; the escaping contract holds (port MessageTest); an on-wiki override beats the file message.
notes: Test: port LocalisationCacheTest, MessageTest, MessageCacheTest. MILESTONE. (Blocked by ws1-s3.) Open Q: store backend (own format vs CDB compat); Leximorph scope; how many LanguageXx subclasses are launch-critical.

title: Breadth: MILESTONE — sessions + authentication (SessionManager + AuthManager + CSRF)
description: IN: SessionManager/SessionBackend/SessionProvider (cookie default), the store-corroboration invariant, CSRF token set (Token/CsrfTokenSet), AuthManager Pre->Primary->Secondary pipeline with the AuthenticationResponse state machine, the local-password primary provider, the re-auth gate. OUT: extension auth providers (OAuth/CentralAuth/2FA), bot-passwords/central-id (defer).
design: includes/Session/SessionManager.php + includes/Auth/AuthManager.php (~117KB). Non-negotiables: never trust request-supplied identity until the session store corroborates userId+userName+userToken (loadSessionInfoFromStore rejects mismatches); CSRF = per-session-secret HMAC with hash_equals (constant-time); account-existence non-leak; only interactive logins count for securitySensitiveOperationStatus.
acceptance_criteria: Session establishment rejects all four corroboration mismatches; the AuthManager state machine pauses/resumes (UI/REDIRECT) with providerIds re-validation; CSRF match is timing-safe.
notes: Test: port SessionManagerTest, AuthManagerTest; CSRF round-trip + tamper tests. MILESTONE. (Blocked by ws2-s3; related ws6-s1.) Open Q: JWT session-cookie path (1.45-era) in v1; SessionStore single vs multi-backend.

title: Breadth: MILESTONE — Authority-equivalent permissions
description: IN: an Authority interface equivalent (the cost/rigor ladder + side-effect semantics), PermissionManager.getPermissionStatus() pipeline, GroupPermissionsLookup (groups->rights, revoke-wins), RestrictionStore (page protection), RateLimiter, PermissionStatus, the Block evaluation junction. OUT: extension auth providers (OAuth/2FA), password-hashing primitives.
design: Mirror includes/Permissions/Authority.php exactly — the isAllowed/probablyCan/definitelyCan/authorize* vocabulary + RIGOR_QUICK|FULL|SECURE mapping is the contract new app code depends on; preserve 'only authorize* increments rate limit' and 'authorizeWrite reads PRIMARY DB'. UserAuthority.php wraps PermissionManager/RateLimiter/BlockManager. Group->rights in GroupPermissionsLookup.php ($wgGroupPermissions/$wgRevokePermissions, revoke always wins). Blocks: BlockManager.php (partial vs sitewide, strictest-wins composite).
acceptance_criteria: Passes a port of UserAuthorityTest (probablyCan false-positive tolerance; rate-limit consumed once per action; write uses primary); group/rights honors revoke-always-wins and session-narrowing-never-widening.
notes: Test: port UserAuthorityTest, PermissionManagerTest, BlockManagerTest; property-test the rigor ladder side-effects. MILESTONE. (Blocked by ws2-s3; related ws6-s2 [shared identity model].) Open Q: Block subsystem depth in v1; temp-user trichotomy at launch.

title: Write: MILESTONE — ChronologyProtector write-side / read-your-writes (runtime-gated)
description: IN: design + implement read-your-writes in the Node model — the request-lifecycle capture point, the position store (micro-stash equivalent), clientId/cookie plumbing, replica-wait on the next request, job requestId inheritance. Starts as a spike (folded into ws5-s1's open questions), promoted to a milestone once WS1's runtime model lands. OUT: the read-side wait itself (ws2-s5).
design: ChronologyProtector.php:268(getSessionPrimaryPos)/298(stageSessionPrimaryPos)/342(persist); LoadBalancer.php:1102/734(primaryPosWait); MediaWikiEntryPoint:309(LBFactory::shutdown PRESEND)/662(SHUTDOWN_NO_CHRONPROT POSTSEND). No PHP session-end hook / implicit cookie-DC routing in Node — needs an explicit Node lifecycle boundary + cookie/clientId plumbing. Shares the cpStash key format + position marshalling with ws2-s5.
acceptance_criteria: After an edit, the same client's immediate next read never sees a stale (pre-edit) replica state, validated against a lagged-replica rig.
notes: Test: inject replica lag; assert post-write read consistency. MILESTONE. (Blocked by ws5-s1.) FULLY GATED on WS1 runtime lifecycle + WS2 LoadBalancer/replica-wait primitive.

title: Write: MILESTONE — PageUpdater-equivalent edit pipeline with page_latest CAS
description: IN: a PageUpdater::saveRevision/doModify/doCreate-equivalent — grabParentRevision CAS token, lockAndGetLatest (SELECT page_latest FOR UPDATE) + revalidate, DOUBLE-CAS on the page UPDATE (page_latest in WHERE), edit-conflict detection, null-edit vs dummy-revision branch, page-row maintenance (page_latest/len/touched/is_redirect/content_model), create-page log entry (logging+log_search, insert WITHOUT publish). OUT: derived data (ws5-s4).
design: PageUpdater.php:1263(doModify)/1314(startAtomic)/1321(CAS compare)/1419(doCreate)/1478-1491(create log without publish); WikiPage.php:2484(lockAndGetLatest FOR UPDATE)/1331-1333(page_latest in UPDATE WHERE)/1355(affectedRows==0 => conflict). The FOR-UPDATE-lock-then-compare must be one atomic unit; a second belt-and-suspenders CAS rides the page UPDATE. CORRECTION vs Epic: the modern path EMITS PageLatestRevisionChangedEvent (EventDispatchEngine) rather than writing side tables inline.
acceptance_criteria: Under N concurrent writers to one page, exactly one wins, losers get edit-conflict, page_latest is NEVER corrupted and points at a real revision; a null edit writes no revision but bumps page_touched; create writes the un-published create log entry.
notes: Test: concurrency harness hammering one page; assert page_latest integrity + one-winner invariant against a shared DB. MILESTONE. (Blocked by ws5-s2.) Needs WS2 row-lock/transaction semantics; WS7 dual-run policy.

title: Write: MILESTONE — core revision insert (revision + slots + content + text/blob + ip_changes)
description: IN: an insertRevisionOn-equivalent — one atomic section writing revision, slots (with slot_origin), content, blob (storeBlob, tt:/es:), ip_changes; main-slot-mandatory + size assertion; inherited-slot reuse (no new blob); NameTable acquireId for slot_role/content_model with transaction-volatility discipline; blob immutability. OUT: page_latest CAS (ws5-s3); derived data (ws5-s4); deferred/runtime tiering (gated on WS1).
design: RevisionStore.php:379/570/646/896/916/682; SlotRecord.php:112(newInherited)/199(newSaved); NameTableStore acquireId is called INSIDE the atomic section, and its IDs are non-cacheable across a transaction boundary (INSERT IGNORE on a separate CONN_TRX_AUTOCOMMIT connection + fallback SELECT); blobs are write-once, never deduped by sha1; inherited slots have slot_origin < slot_revision_id and reuse the parent content row+address.
acceptance_criteria: Dual-write of an edit fixture set produces byte-identical revision/slots/content/text/ip_changes rows to PHP, incl. correct slot_origin for inherited slots and correct rev_len/rev_sha1/content_sha1; INSERT-IGNORE + fallback-SELECT race behavior matches; no orphaned/duplicate normalization rows under concurrent insert.
notes: Test: fixtures from ws5-s1; concurrency test inserting the same new role/model name from two writers. MILESTONE. (Blocked by ws5-s1, ws2-s3.) Needs WS2 DBAL atomic-section + autocommit-side-connection semantics.

title: API: Action API framework core + first read module (action=query + one prop submodule)
description: IN: ApiMain lifecycle (setupExecuteAction->checkAsserts->setupModule->checkExecutePermissions->execute->reportUnusedParams->printResult), ApiModuleManager (ObjectFactory dispatch), ApiResult (metadata-annotated tree + size limiting), ApiFormatJson with formatversion=1 BC transforms, ApiErrorFormatter(_BackCompat), ApiQuery + ApiPageSet + ONE prop submodule (ApiQueryInfo or ApiQueryRevisions), continuation (ApiContinuationManager). OUT: generators breadth, write modules (WS5), help/paraminfo (defer), xml/php/none formatters (defer), the other ~150 modules (ws4-s7).
design: The unbreakable shape (verified): ApiFormatJson.php::execute default transforms (BC=[], AssocAsObject, Strip:all, XMLMETA_OK \u-escaping); ApiResult.php metadata constants (_type/_content(->*)/_element/_BC_bools); ApiMain.php envelope (warnings/errors/legacy error/batchcomplete/requestid/servedby/curtimestamp); ApiQuery.php (query.pages + normalized/redirects). ApiQueryRevisions consumes RevisionStore + SlotRoleRegistry (WS2 MCR) + ContentRenderer (WS3 render).
acceptance_criteria: api.php?action=query&...&format=json (default formatversion=1) output byte-matches PHP for a fixture request — boolean-as-empty-string, * content key, \u escaping, key ordering, continue/batchcomplete placement, warnings/errors envelope.
notes: Test: port tests/api-testing/action/ fixtures (Links.js, Backlinks.js) + a golden-byte corpus captured from PHP for formatversion 1 and 2. (Blocked by ws4-s1 [shared ParamValidator], ws2-s8, ws3-s3.) Open Q: exact key-ordering and \u-escaping parity with FormatJson::encode (top contract risk — pin with the byte corpus first).

title: Runtime: logging & observability foundation (PSR-3 loggers, stats + tracing seams)
description: IN: a LoggerFactory-equivalent — pluggable SPI returning channel-named structured loggers (getInstance(channel)), a request-scoped LoggingContext, config-driven provider selection; interface-only seams for stats (StatsFactory: counters/gauges/timings/histograms) and tracing (Tracer/span), wired into the request lifecycle (root span per request). OUT: concrete stats/tracing backends — provide interfaces + a no-op default; concrete emitters are later/breadth.
design: includes/Logger/LoggerFactory.php — static SPI via ObjectFactory, LoggingContext (1.44). 110 distinct logger channels across includes/ (rdbms, runJobs, replication, session, ...) — the taxonomy is worth preserving for parity. Root-span lifecycle: Setup.php:338-362 (per web request, backdated to REQUEST_TIME_FLOAT), ended in restInPeace (:664). In the resident model the per-request span must be request-local (ties ws1-s2). StatsFactory is injected into 20+ services — publish the token early so downstream workstreams can depend on it.
acceptance_criteria: getLogger('rdbms') returns a channel-tagged structured logger; provider swappable via config; request-scoped context fields appear on all events within a request and not across requests; a root span is created per request and ended on completion.
notes: Test: unit on SPI swap + channel tagging + context isolation; integration on span-per-request lifecycle. Open Q: PSR-3 npm equivalent vs custom interface; OpenTelemetry for the tracing seam.

title: Cutover: MILESTONE — PHP retirement (Parsoid sidecar retained)
description: IN: remove/retire the PHP entry-point scripts once every surface is cut over and stable (index.php, api.php, rest.php, load.php, thumb.php/thumb_handler.php, img_auth.php, opensearch_desc.php, maintenance/run.php) + the PHP includes/ runtime; RETAIN the Parsoid sidecar (wikimedia/parsoid, still called by the TS engine) + the shared DB schema; keep the parity harnesses (ws7-s1/s2) as the regression net through and after retirement. OUT: schema changes; Parsoid replacement.
design: Entry points = root *.php. Parsoid is a SEPARATE package and the strategic render engine (handbook ch.10 decision #6) — it survives retirement by design (Epic: 'leaving the Parsoid sidecar'). maintenance/run.php (the CLI hub) and mw-config/ (installer) are PHP surfaces that need TS equivalents before removal.
acceptance_criteria: No PHP entry point is reachable in production (all traffic served by TS); the Parsoid sidecar is still callable + used by the TS render path; the parity harnesses are still green at retirement; the schema/data is untouched and an operator update-equivalent path exists.
notes: Test: full e2e across all surfaces with PHP removed; parity-rate must hold. MILESTONE. (Blocked by ws7-s3, ws7-s4.) Open Q: TS equivalent for maintenance/run.php + mw-config/ installer scope; whether any PHP maintenance scripts persist transitionally.

title: Cutover: MILESTONE — dual-write safety gate (single-writer enforcement + shadow-write parity)
description: IN: enforce that only ONE engine writes at a time per surface during cutover (no concurrent PHP+TS writes to the same tables); a verification mode that shadow-runs TS writes against a snapshot/clone and diffs the resulting rows (esp. revision/slots/content + any table mid-SCHEMA_COMPAT_* migration) before granting a write surface for ws7-s3. Consumes WS5's shared-DB write invariants. OUT: routing (ws7-s3); read parity (ws7-s1/s2).
design: CORRECTION vs Epic: dual-WRITE on a shared DB is UNSAFE — two engines would each independently drive PageUpdater/RevisionStore/deferred updates and the SCHEMA_COMPAT_* transitions with no cross-engine coordination. SCHEMA_COMPAT_{WRITE,READ}_{OLD,TEMP,NEW} flags: includes/Defines.php:293-306; the 7-stage migration + 'no plain ALTER on billion-row tables' (handbook ch.10). File tables + linktarget are actively mid-migration — a second uncoordinated writer corrupts the staged sequence. Reuse the cloned-temp-table discipline (handbook ch.06) for shadow-write verification. CUTOVER MUST BE READ-ONLY-FIRST.
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent PHP+TS write to the same surface is structurally prevented (single-writer assertion); shadow-write mode produces a row-level diff vs the PHP baseline; a write surface cannot cut over (ws7-s3) without a passing dual-write parity report; tables under active SCHEMA_COMPAT_* migration are explicitly handled.
notes: Test: integration on a cloned DB; assert single-writer guard; row-diff golden test on revision/slots. MILESTONE. (Blocked by ws5-s3.) Open Q: per-table write-parity tolerance; freeze active schema migrations during the cutover window.

title: Cutover: MILESTONE — progressive per-surface cutover routing (read-only-first)
description: IN: a routing/front-controller shim that sends each entry-point surface (index.php views, rest.php, api.php, load.php, thumb.php/thumb_handler.php, img_auth.php, opensearch_desc.php) to PHP or TS, per-surface and reversible; sequencing READ-ONLY surfaces first (index.php GET views, rest.php GETs, load.php, thumb.php, opensearch_desc.php), gated by ws7-s1/s2 parity rates; write surfaces last, only after the dual-write gate (ws7-s4). OUT: the dual-write safety mechanism (ws7-s4); the parity harnesses (ws7-s1/s2).
design: CORRECTION vs Epic: there is NO in-repo traffic-routing/shadowing layer (handbook ch.07 — routing is Wikimedia infra), so this shim is NET-NEW. Surfaces enumerated from root *.php + root AGENTS.md. The read/write split mirrors the replica/primary discipline ($dbr/$dbw).
acceptance_criteria: Each surface flips PHP<->TS independently and rolls back; write surfaces are blocked from cutover until the ws7-s4 gate is satisfied; a surface's cutover is gated on a configurable parity-rate threshold from ws7-s1/s2.
notes: Test: e2e smoke per surface post-flip; integration test of the flip/rollback switch. MILESTONE. (Blocked by ws7-s1, ws7-s2, ws7-s4.) Open Q: routing layer location (reverse proxy vs PHP front controller); per-wiki vs global granularity.

title: Breadth: MILESTONE — special-page framework + operational maintenance CLI
description: IN: the SpecialPage base lifecycle (run->beforeExecute->execute->afterExecute) + permission helpers, SpecialPageFactory (registration/alias/dispatch), the operational special pages (Search, UserLogin/CreateAccount/Logout, RecentChanges/Watchlist, ListFiles); the Maintenance base class + run.php runner + the OPERATIONAL script subset (~12-15). OUT: the ~185 non-operational scripts; the full ~200-page special-page roster (mostly reporting QueryPages — port on demand).
design: includes/SpecialPage/SpecialPage.php + SpecialPageFactory.php (config-driven registration, ObjectFactory specs, alias resolution); maintenance/includes/Maintenance.php + maintenance/run.php; schema/install engine update.php::UpdateMediaWiki -> includes/Installer/DatabaseUpdater.php. CORRECTION vs Epic: the operational maintenance subset is SMALL (~12-15 of 202): install/update(+DatabaseUpdater), generateSchemaSql/generateSchemaChangeSql, sql/patchSql, runJobs, rebuildLocalisationCache, refreshLinks, updateSearchIndex/rebuildtextindex, createAndPromote, importDump.
acceptance_criteria: A registered special page dispatches with permission/header checks; alias resolution + canonical 301 (GET) works; install/update bootstrap a fresh schema and apply migrations via the DatabaseUpdater equivalent; runJobs/rebuildLocalisationCache/refreshLinks execute end-to-end.
notes: Test: port SpecialPageTest/SpecialPageFactoryTest; integration-test the install->update->runJobs loop on a temp DB. MILESTONE. (Blocked by ws6-s3 [aliases/messages], ws1-s6.) Open Q: which special pages are launch-critical vs the reporting long-tail.

title: Breadth: MILESTONE — job workers (JobRunner + JobQueue backend)
description: IN: the WORKER side — JobRunner claim->run->commit->deferred-flush->ack loop, JobQueue/JobQueueGroup consumption, a JobQueueDB-equivalent backend, JobFactory (type->class registry), JobSpecification serialization, the runJobs operational entry, idempotency/at-least-once + bounded retry. OUT: job ENQUEUE on the write path + the deferred-updates->job fallback (WS5); the actual job BODIES (RefreshLinksJob etc. ship from their owning subsystems).
design: includes/JobQueue/JobRunner.php + JobQueueGroup.php + JobQueueDB.php. Worker invariants: jobs idempotent (at-least-once, order undefined); each runs in its own transaction round + post-job deferred-update flush; the runner stops on replica lag >=3s or memory >=95%; retry up to maxTries (default 3). COORDINATE-not-duplicate with WS5: WS5 owns lazyPush/push + the EnqueueableDataUpdate->job bridge; WS6 owns pop+execute. The shared contract is the JobSpecification (type + JSON params) — agree it once.
acceptance_criteria: A pushed job (spec from WS5's enqueue) is popped, run idempotently, acked; a throwing job retries up to maxTries; the runner honors lag/memory stop conditions.
notes: Test: port JobQueueTest + JobRunner loop tests; idempotency + retry-bound integration with a stub job. MILESTONE. (Blocked by ws1-s5; related ws5-s4 [enqueue/JobSpecification seam].) Open Q: backend in v1 (DB only vs Redis); who owns the JobSpecification format.

title: Breadth: MILESTONE — core SearchEngine + DB backend + index maintenance
description: IN: the SearchEngine abstract surface, SearchEngineFactory auto-resolution from DB type, ONE DB backend (SQL MATCH...AGAINST/FTS over a searchindex-equivalent), PrefixSearch/TitleMatcher near-match, the SearchUpdate index-maintenance hook + an updateSearchIndex/rebuildtextindex operational path, result-set/suggestion value objects. OUT: CirrusSearch/Elasticsearch (out-of-scope extension); advanced relevance ranking; SearchEngineDummy is the floor for unsupported DBs.
design: CORRECTION vs Epic (materially important): core ships REAL DB-backed search, NOT delegated to CirrusSearch. $wgSearchType defaults to null (MainConfigSchema::SearchType); SearchEngineFactory::getSearchEngineClass auto-selects SearchMySQL/SearchSqlite/SearchPostgres from the live connection (else SearchEngineDummy). CirrusSearch is an extension that OVERRIDES the search-type config — keep the factory override seam. So search can't be skipped, but Elasticsearch-grade relevance is explicitly OUT — scope to DB-fallback parity.
acceptance_criteria: Title + full-text query over seeded content returns results via the DB backend; prefix/near-match works; index stays current on edit; an unsupported DB degrades to dummy (no crash).
notes: Test: port SearchEngineTest + the SQL-backend search tests; seed-and-query integration. MILESTONE. (Blocked by ws2-s3.) Open Q: keep the searchindex table + SearchUpdate wiring or stub index maintenance until a search extension lands; FTS dialect parity.

title: Breadth: MILESTONE — files subsystem (FileBackend -> FileRepo -> File + media handlers + thumb/img_auth)
description: IN: the framework-agnostic FileBackend (FS backend min), FileRepo/LocalRepo policy (zones, hash sharding, virtual URLs), File/LocalFile, RepoGroup, MediaHandlerFactory + a raster handler chain, thumbnail-on-demand entry (thumb.php) with the rel404 hash verification + PoolCounter/failure-counter stampede guard, protected-file entry (img_auth.php). OUT: Swift/object-store (FS-only v1), foreign repos (Commons), audio/video handlers (extensions), the upload FRONTEND (Special:Upload/ApiUpload).
design: Keep the FileBackend(lib)/FileRepo(policy)/LocalFile(DB) layer discipline (includes/libs/filebackend/FileBackend.php, includes/FileRepo/FileRepo.php, FileRepo/File/LocalFile.php). Respect the live schema migration image/oldimage->file/filerevision via a FileSelectQueryBuilder gated on the WS2-chosen file-schema stage ($wgFileSchemaMigrationStage). Thumbnailing shells out via a hardened wrapper; preserve the $wgMaxImageArea decompression-bomb guard + the T36231 rel404 anti-CDN-poison check.
acceptance_criteria: Round-trip upload->store->thumbnail->stream on FS backend; hash-path/zone-URL derivations match; thumb 404 path renders+caches+streams; img_auth denies without read.
notes: Test: port FileRepoTest, LocalFileTest, FileBackendTest, UploadBaseTest (verification subset). MILESTONE. (Blocked by ws2-s3, ws1-s6.) Open Q: which file-schema stage (depends on WS2); Swift in v1; upload trust-boundary checks here or split with the upload frontend.

title: Write: MILESTONE (decision-gated) — incremental derived counters
description: IN: the non-idempotent counter set — category.cat_pages/cat_subcats/cat_files (async CategoryCountUpdateJob), change_tag_def.ctd_count, site_stats.ss_total_*, user.user_editcount; DECIDE ownership (route through identical exactly-once jobs vs leave to PHP entirely); implement only AFTER the dual-run decision. OUT: everything else.
design: EXPANSION vs Epic (the Epic missed all of these — the worst shared-DB hazard): CategoryCountUpdateJob.php:120-124 (field +/- 1 RawSQL, async job); ChangeTagsStore.php:701-707 (+1 via onTransactionPreCommitOrIdle); SiteStatsUpdate (RawSQL deltas); UserEditTracker (POSTSEND increment). These have NO transactional coupling to the row they count — concurrent/duplicated increments from two engines silently drift them with no error.
acceptance_criteria: Under dual-run, no counter drifts vs ground-truth COUNT(*); no double-increment across engines.
notes: Test: long-running concurrent edit soak; periodic counter-vs-COUNT reconciliation. MILESTONE. (Blocked by ws5-s5.) DECISION-FIRST: WS7 dual-run write policy + 'who owns counters' must be resolved before any code.

title: Write: MILESTONE — derived data (links family, page_props, categorylinks, parser-cache invalidation)
description: IN: a LinksUpdate-equivalent diff machinery for pagelinks/templatelinks/imagelinks/externallinks/langlinks/iwlinks/existencelinks/categorylinks/page_props; ParserCache SAVE-THROUGH invalidation (write a fresh entry, not delete); recursive-vs-inline split (page inline, backlinks -> job). OUT: recentchanges/tags (ws5-s5); incremental counters (ws5-s6); the PRESEND/POSTSEND scheduling tier (gated on WS1 ws1-s5).
design: LinksUpdate.php:212/233(queueRecursiveJobs); PagePropsTable encodeValue:117 (bool->1/0, null->''); CategoryLinksTable (cl_sortkey/cl_type via normalized linktarget); DerivedPageDataUpdater doParserCacheUpdate:1790 (parserCache->save — warm, not purge). Invalidates WS3's Parsoid ParserCache — must write the cache WS3 reads (agree the two-key scheme + key format).
acceptance_criteria: After a dual-write edit, all link/page_props/categorylinks rows are byte-identical to PHP (correct encodeValue, sortkeys, cl_type); the ParserCache for the new revision is written, not purged; re-running on unchanged content makes zero row changes.
notes: Test: fixtures from ws5-s1; diff-update churn test. MILESTONE. (Blocked by ws5-s3, ws1-s5.) Needs WS3 ParserCache key/format contract.

title: Write: MILESTONE — change-tracking event subscriber (recentchanges + change_tag + EditResult)
description: IN: event-driven RC insert (rc_actor/rc_comment dedup, rc_source/oldids), EditResult classification (null/new/revert + auto revert-tags mw-undo/mw-rollback/mw-manual-revert), change_tag/change_tag_def writes, user_newtalk on user-talk edits; replicate the post-commit/cancel-on-rollback dispatch contract. OUT: counters (ws5-s6).
design: CORRECTION/EXPANSION vs Epic: the write path is EVENT-DRIVEN. PageUpdater emits PageLatestRevisionChangedEvent (emitEvents:1368/1502, queued inside the atomic section); EventDispatchEngine::dispatch wraps each listener in an MWCallableUpdate bound to $dbw that runs post-commit but auto-cancels on rollback (EventDispatchEngine.php:184-198). recentchanges is NOT written by the core save path — RecentChangeStore::insertRecentChange (:147) runs from the deferred listener (ChangeTrackingEventIngress) with its own actor/comment dedup. A dual-engine TS writer must replicate the transactional-coupling-without-in-transaction-execution contract.
acceptance_criteria: A dual-write edit produces byte-identical recentchanges + change_tag rows; revert detection matches PHP's EditResult; creation produces no duplicate RC row (log-without-publish honored).
notes: Test: fixtures incl. undo/rollback/manual-revert; assert tag + rc parity. MILESTONE. (Blocked by ws5-s3, ws1-s5.) Needs WS1 dispatch/deferred model; WS7 dual-run (RC double-write risk).

title: API: MILESTONE — Action API breadth (remaining read modules + formatters + help)
description: IN (coarse): the remaining prop/list/meta read submodules + generators; ApiFormatXml/Php/None/Raw/FeedWrapper; formatversion=2/latest parity; action=help/paraminfo generation; maxlag/CORS/conditional-request at full fidelity. OUT: write modules (WS5).
design: ApiModuleManager constants + $wgAPI*Modules; ApiQuery.php group registration; help machinery (ApiHelp/ApiParamInfo).
acceptance_criteria: Each module byte-matches its tests/api-testing/action/ fixture for both formatversion 1 and 2.
notes: Test: per-module contract tests. MILESTONE. (Blocked by ws4-s5; needs WS2/WS3 per module.)

title: API: MILESTONE — REST breadth (revision/history/transform/media/search handlers)
description: IN (coarse): remaining core REST handlers — RevisionSource/HTMLHandler, PageHistory(Count)Handler, CompareHandler, LanguageLinksHandler, MediaFile/MediaLinksHandler, SearchHandler, the Transform/Parsoid family, sitemap handlers, ActionModuleBasedHandler bridge; per-endpoint vertical (route+handler+contract test). Sequence by client demand (Wikimedia apps first).
design: All in includes/Rest/Handler/; contract fixtures in tests/api-testing/REST/. The Transform family depends on WS3's Parsoid sidecar. ActionModuleBasedHandler transitively depends on ws4-s5 (Action framework).
acceptance_criteria: Each ported endpoint byte-matches its tests/api-testing/REST/ fixture.
notes: Test: per-endpoint contract tests. MILESTONE — decompose finely when each endpoint is scheduled. (Blocked by ws4-s1; needs WS3 for Transform, WS2 for revision/history.)
